seo.description: The ramparts of the Portuguese City of El Jadida — wall circuit facing the ocean, bastions and period cannons. UNESCO World Heritage.
seo.og_description: Ocean-facing walls, bastions and cannons of the 16th-century Portuguese citadel.

name: Ramparts & Bastions
hero_subtitle: Walk the walls above the Atlantic — cannons, bastions and open horizons.

overview.title: Massive walls above the ocean
overview.p1: The massive walls of the Portuguese City, built in the 16th century, rise directly from the Atlantic. Walking the circuit offers constant views of the sea, the port and the rooftops of the medina.
overview.p2: Bastions, ramparts and period cannons punctuate the route. The light at the end of the day is particularly beautiful for photos.
overview.p3: The walk is easy and free. Combine it with the cistern and the Church of the Assumption for a complete visit of the citadel.

q1.question: How much time for Ramparts?
q1.answer: 30 to 60 minutes is usually enough for a good visit.

q2.question: Is there an entry fee?
q2.answer: Many outdoor areas are free; the cistern has a ticket. Check on site.

q3.question: Can I visit with children?
q3.answer: Yes, most sites are suitable for families with basic supervision.

q4.question: Is it open every day?
q4.answer: Outdoor sites are generally accessible daily; indoor sites may close one day a week.

q5.question: Do I need a guide?
q5.answer: Not required, but a local guide enriches the history of the Portuguese City.
